¡ Any condition that causes the pipeline to 
stall is called a hazard.
¡
Result: Much bubbles and degraded efficiency
¡ Various types of hazards
¡
Data Hazard: Stall due to dependencies of some 
data
¡
Read-after-write (RAW)
¡
Write-after-write (WAW)
¡
Write-after-read (WAR)
¡
Control Hazard: Stall due to branch and 
synchronization
¡
Structural hazard: Stall due to contention on 
hardware such as memory channel, cache slot, 
queue, etc.
CPU: Optimize Latency of a Small Number of Complex Threads
Why Pipeline Stalls: Hazards

¡ Enable Register-to-Register or Register-to-ALU Forwarding 
¡
E.g., result is passed directly from pipeline register to ALU input. 
¡
The consumer can execute earlier ——> Fewer stalls and higher pipeline efficiency

1 - f: serial fraction
p: number of processors / threads

different execution path
¡ Result: Only a subset of threads execute, 
waste SIMD pipeline utilization

CPU: Optimize Latency of a Small Number of Complex Threads
Optimization #6: OoO Superscalar with Hyper-Threading
¡ Problem: Even OoO superscalar cores have idle slot issues.
¡ Reasons: 
¡
Cache miss, branch misprediction, dependency chain……
¡ Hyper-threading introduces simultaneous multithreading (SMT)
¡
Multiple hardware threads share one physical core.
¡
Each logical thread has its own architectural state.
¡
Execution units, caches, queues, and predictors are shared.
¡ The closest architecture to modern CPUs.

From CPU to GPU: Parallelism for Huge Computing Power!
¡ Parallelism: Do multiple jobs concurrently.
¡
Job: instructions, operations, tasks
¡ Data Parallelism
¡
Different pieces of data can be operated in parallel
¡
Vector processing and array processing
¡ Task Parallelism
¡
Different tasks can be operated in parallel
¡
Multithreading 
Multiprocessors

CPU Multicore Programming: pThread
¡ Mutex pattern:
Mutex: Protect Shared State
pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
sum += local_sum;
pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
¡ The Mutex provides:
¡ Serialized access to critical section 
¡ Race avoidance for protected 
shared state 
¡ Cost: Lock contention
Only one thread holds the mutex; others wait and the protected region is serialized
